A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GDGB benchmark, TDGG/IDGG tasks, and GAG-General framework. Their readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable matching across the reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original graph-generation experiments, comparisons with DGNNs and generative baselines, memory/reflection ablations, and scalability measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains these experiments and adds downstream utility results, DTGB generation experiments, semantic-drift tests, and human evaluations.

M1.justification: The core pipeline, Algorithms 1–2, memory/reflection components, and base generation prompts are retained. V2 Section F.14 additionally evaluates guided generation with domain constraints inserted into node and edge prompts, a limited adaptation of the inference procedure.

E1.justification: The eight GDGB datasets remain unchanged. V2 extends TDGG/IDGG evaluation to all eight DTGB datasets, previously used for structural/text-feature comparisons, and adds generated-graph substitution and cold-start inductive link-prediction scenarios on Sephora, WikiLife, Cora, and WeiboTech (C.5, F.5, F.12).

E2.justification: V2 Tables 8 and 53 add TIGGER-I to the IDGG comparison against VRDAG and DG-Gen in v1 Tables 10 and 46. The existing LLM backbones and DGNN comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: V2 introduces generated-versus-original graph controls, augmentation controls with Average Precision evaluation, intrinsic text-quality measurements, and a 10,000-edge semantic-drift protocol using ten snapshots. Human evaluation uses five annotators and 50 sampled nodes with interactions. The hub case changes from 5,000 to 2,000 edges; core generation budgets and splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Existing memory/reflection ablations, text-feature comparisons, and scalability analyses are retained. V2 adds substantial analyses of intrinsic textual quality, downstream synthetic-data utility, semantic drift with constrained-prompt controls, and human-perceived realism and contextual consistency (C.5, F.5, F.12–F.15).

E5.justification: V1 reports point estimates only. V2 Tables 31, 32, and 54 introduce ± uncertainty terms for downstream results, but do not specify their statistical meaning, run counts, or seeds. This establishes a reporting change without establishing additional repeated runs.

E6.justification: Matched core result tables retain their values. V2 adds DTGB generation results, TIGGER-I scores, downstream utility results, drift curves, and human ratings. For example, Table 54 reports augmentation AP gains of 0.027–0.108, and Table 55 reports GPT-based Sephora node/edge human scores of 3.9/4.3. Hub examples are replaced under a different graph size.

T1.justification: V2 Section F.14 introduces mathematical definitions for pooled snapshot semantic representations and consecutive-snapshot cosine similarity, Equations 1–2. Existing task definitions and structural/embedding metric formulations are retained; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: an eight-dataset generative DyTAG benchmark, TDGG/IDGG tasks, multifaceted metrics, GAG-General, and the importance of structural and textual information. Additional evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands interpretations of practical utility and semantic quality: synthetic graphs are evaluated as substitutes and augmentation data, and semantic usefulness is distinguished from text length. Section F.14 newly identifies off-domain generation after approximately 5,000 edges and interprets prompt constraints as mitigation, adding a concrete applicability limitation absent from v1.

D1.justification: V2 supplies previously omitted evaluator prompts, detailed scoring rubrics, response formats, and dataset contexts in G.3, and specifies fixed evaluator hyperparameters in D.3/E.4. These substantially improve documentation of a central evaluation component. Most generation settings, hardware details, and generation templates were already present in v1.

R1.justification: V2 expands the targeted positioning against DTGB and explains GAG-General’s relationship to GAG in C.5/D.1. References to EvolveGCN, ROLAND, and Disentangled Dynamic Graph Deep Generation are removed. TIGGER was already cited in v1; its new experimental participation is separate from citation changes.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much technical prose remain intact. V2 revises introductory, results, and future-work passages, adds an appendix contents list and disclosure statements, and reorganizes appendix material, including moving Broader Impact to the opening Ethics Statement.

P2.justification: V2 adds the text-quality radar chart, hub visualizations, semantic-drift plots, and substantial new comparison, utility, human-evaluation, and evaluator-prompt tables. Earlier figures and discriminative result summaries are relocated or consolidated into appendices, alongside extensive conference-format layout changes.

improvement.justification: V1 largely left synthetic-data utility prospective and assessed generated text through an LLM evaluator. V2 adds direct utility and augmentation tests, human assessment, and semantic-drift diagnosis with mitigation controls, while disclosing the evaluator prompts. These substantially strengthen practical validation, failure characterization, and reproducibility. Underspecified downstream protocols and undefined ± statistics limit the new evidence but do not outweigh these gains.
